title: The claim/release state machine of an agent task list, in three languages
pins: Who may hold a task, when a lease has lapsed, who may release it, and the bytes of the stored record. A task list is DURABLE state that outlives the process which wrote it, and nothing says the process reading it back is in the same language -- so the list itself is the shared surface. A one-tick disagreement about expiry hands one task to two workers. A disagreement about how claimed_by is compared lets one worker close another's work. Neither errors, and both look like ordinary operation.
scope: The claim and release paths, and the canonical record. NOT the completion tool, NOT lease extension, and NOT the store's locking primitive -- each is a separate value with its own failure mode, and this suite existing does not cover them. The generator's store uses a no-op lock deliberately: the lock has its own defects, three of which were found and fixed while this feature was built, and measuring them here would conflate two things.
construction: Each row seeds a list state DIRECTLY rather than through add(), so a row may describe a state the public API would refuse to build -- an inconsistent one, say. A corpus that can only express states the implementation is willing to create cannot test what it does when it meets one it did not. Time is frozen per row, so expiry boundaries are exact rather than raced.
findings: TypeScript is RUN and COMPARED, and it was not the exception: the suite found a hole in prism-harness-ts on its first run, at atc-0011 and atc-0012. The port had NO RUNTIME OUTCOME GUARD on release() -- TaskOutcome is a compile-time union in TypeScript, so an outcome that is not `done` or `failed` was written into the durable list as a state that is not one of the four, and nothing refused until a reader mapped the row back. That refusal, `unmappable_content`, then fires for EVERY language that opens the list, so the port that reported the failure was not the port that caused it. The reference and Python both refuse at the door, through a runtime enum, and were never affected. CLOSED 2026-09-04 by a runtime guard in release(); both rows now agree and G-39 is closed. The rows were recorded as divergences FIRST and the fix came second, deliberately: a row that only ever existed green proves nothing about the guard that makes it green, and the runner still hands the outcome over unvalidated so the guard is measured rather than supplied. TypeScript now agrees on all 20 rows the reference can express. Python is RUN and COMPARED too, and the suite found a second defect on ITS first run -- atc-0017, the fractional lease, which for a few hours had three answers. PHP SKIPS it under 0002 because claim() declares ?int and the type system rejects 90.4 before any guard runs; TypeScript REFUSED it as task_lease_invalid; and Python ACCEPTED it and truncated to 90, landing claimed_until on now+90 -- the silent configuration change the row's title says must not happen, in the unsafe direction, since a lease that lapses early hands the task out while its holder still believes it holds it. Neither language's own suite could see it: the reference cannot even ask the question, and each port asserts against the value its own code produced. CLOSED 2026-09-04 in prism-harness-py by requiring a positive WHOLE number of seconds at every door, including the configuration route; G-40 is closed. Recorded as a divergence first and fixed second, for the same reason G-39 was. All three languages now agree on every row either can express, and atc-0017 is a shape difference rather than a behaviour one: PHP is skipped by its signature, both ports refuse by decision. Two things recorded before any port ran and both still hold: atc-0015 shows duplicate ids are guarded at add() and TOLERATED on read, so a list written by a less careful port is accepted and find() resolves the id to whichever comes first; and the reachable PHP path for a fractional lease is the configuration route, which is a different value and belongs in its own row.
construction_note: The generator's seeding writes to the source's OWN key. An earlier version wrote to the bare list name, so every row read an empty list and the generator recorded 'nothing happened' for all 21 as though it were an answer -- outcome ok, pending 0, no record, entirely plausible. It now asserts the source can see the tasks it was given and exits loudly if it cannot. A generator that silently measures nothing is the defect this repository exists to catch, one level up.

ts.note: Full as of 2026-09-04: agrees with the reference on all 20 rows it can express, and ANSWERS atc-0017 rather than inheriting PHP's skip -- a fractional lease reaches assertLease and is refused as task_lease_invalid, this port's own decision rather than its type system's. It was not full on arrival. atc-0011 and atc-0012 were recorded as divergences first and closed by G-39, a runtime outcome guard in StoreTaskSource.release(); the runner still passes the outcome through UNVALIDATED, which is what keeps those two rows a test of that guard rather than of the type annotation in front of it.

py.note: Full as of 2026-09-04: agrees with the reference on all 20 rows it can express, agrees with prism-harness-ts on all 21, and ANSWERS atc-0017 rather than inheriting PHP's skip -- a fractional lease reaches _require_lease and is refused as task_lease_invalid, this port's own decision rather than its type system's. It was not full on arrival. atc-0017 was recorded as a divergence FIRST, showing this port accepting 90.4 and truncating it to a 90 second lease, and the fix came second: a row that only ever existed green proves nothing about the guard that makes it green. _require_lease asked for finite-and-positive and not for WHOLE, so the lease was a configuration silently becoming a different configuration -- in the UNSAFE direction, since a lease that lapses early hands the task out while its holder still believes it holds it. Closed by requiring a positive whole number at every door, with a test on the configuration route (Session.tasks) and not only on direct calls, because the reference's own guard was defeated from inside its shipped config file by an (int) cast. G-40, closed.
